summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, HIV, and recent MRSA catheter infection was admitted for persistent blurry vision following anesthesia for a venogram and symptomatic hypotension after dialysis. Ophthalmology attributed the vision changes to transient loss of accommodation, expected to resolve with time and managed with reading glasses. Hypotension improved with IV fluids and resumption of midodrine. She developed dysphagia suggestive of candidal esophagitis, treated with a 14-day course of fluconazole. Due to catheter clotting and underlying IVC stenosis, warfarin was initiated for anticoagulation. She remained stable throughout the admission, completed a dialysis session without issues, and was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up in ophthalmology, dermatology, allergy, and primary care, along with continued antibiotic and anticoagulant therapy.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
